security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown examples, TypeScript template strings, relative imports, or documented environment-variable usage. One real issue remains: references/testing.md recommends a curl-to-bash installer command, which is unsafe because it executes unverified remote content.

remediation.issue: Unsafe remote installer command in testing documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-bash Maestro installation example with a package manager command, official manual install steps, or checksum/signature verification instructions.

content.user_title: Build React Native Apps with Expo Guidance
content.value_statement: React Native projects often need many platform-specific decisions across navigation, UI, performance, and releases. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise patterns for Expo apps from setup to shipping.
actual_capabilities: Guides Expo Router setup with stack, tabs, route files, and navigation patterns.
Recommends React Native UI choices for lists, images, safe areas, gestures, and platform-specific components.
Provides patterns for styling with NativeWind, themes, spacing, typography, and responsive layouts.
Covers state, forms, networking, server routes, environment variables, and authentication examples.
Explains performance profiling, bundle analysis, animation constraints, testing, and EAS release workflows.
limitations: It is a guidance skill, not a project generator or automatic migration tool.
It cannot verify behavior on physical devices without a separate app run or manual test.
Some guidance depends on current Expo SDK support and platform release constraints.
Native module advice may require checking each library's latest documentation.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Expo App
use_cases.description: Use the skill to choose project structure, Expo Router layout, core dependencies, and early performance defaults.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing React Native Features
use_cases.description: Use the references to improve lists, forms, networking, animations, and styling without broad rewrites.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Mobile Release
use_cases.description: Use the testing, performance, CI, and EAS guidance to check readiness before App Store or Play Store submission.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Expo App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the react-native-dev skill to outline the first steps for a new Expo TypeScript app with Expo Router.

prompt_templates.title: Choose UI Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the react-native-dev skill to recommend React Native components for a feed screen with images, safe areas, and press states.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Performance Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the react-native-dev skill to review this screen for list jank, slow startup causes, and animation performance problems.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Release Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the react-native-dev skill to create a release checklist for testing, profiling, EAS builds, environment variables, and store submission.

output_examples.input: How should I structure a new Expo Router app?
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan covering app routes, root layout, tab layout, path aliases, safe area handling, and recommended dependencies.

output_examples.input: My product list stutters on Android.
output_examples.output: A focused diagnosis that recommends FlashList, memoized rows, stable callbacks, image caching, and profiling in a production-like build.

output_examples.input: What should I check before shipping?
output: Build and submit with EAS profiles.

best_practices: Consult the relevant reference file before changing navigation, networking, testing, or release behavior.
Prefer Expo-supported libraries and direct imports unless a native requirement forces a custom build.
Validate UI changes on a simulator or device because type checks cannot prove mobile behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad React Native defaults when the skill recommends Expo-specific alternatives.
Do not optimize performance before measuring in a production-like build.
Do not place reusable components, utilities, or types inside Expo Router route directories.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete app automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides implementation choices and examples while Claude, Codex, or Claude Code edits your project.

faq.question: Is it focused on Expo or bare React Native?
faq.answer: It focuses on Expo and Expo Router, with React Native patterns that also help many bare projects.

faq.question: Can it help with performance problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers list rendering, startup time, animation constraints, memory profiling, and bundle analysis.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes unit, component, integration, and E2E testing guidance for React Native and Expo apps.

faq.question: Can it manage secrets safely?
faq.answer: It explains public Expo variables and server-only secrets, but you must verify your project configuration.

faq.question: Should I use it for native Swift or Kotlin apps?
faq.answer: No. It is for React Native and Expo. Use platform-specific guidance for native iOS or Android apps.
